title: blm
description: A collection of Bureau of Land Management (BLM) National MLRS/EGIS case-record layers covering federal onshore land tenure and mineral activity: oil and gas leases and agreements, coal, geothermal, oil shale, non-energy leasables, mineral materials, mining claims, locatable operations, rights-of-way, land-use leases and permits, and land acquisitions. It also includes grazing allotments, Utah special tar sand areas and the Utah federal mineral estate. Each layer is published as GeoParquet, PMTiles and H3 hex.

## acquisitions__README.md # BLM National MLRS Acquisitions with H3 Indexing Lands and interests in land **acquired by** the Bureau of Land Management, nationwide, from its National MLRS / EGIS program. 97,529 polygon case records converted to cloud-native formats (GeoParquet, PMTiles, H3 hex) with parcel-level H3 indexing at resolution 10. This is the land-*tenure* half of the non-mineral MLRS records — how BLM-administered land came to be held. It covers purchases, donations and transfers under authorities such as the Taylor Grazing Act, Bankhead-Jones, the Migratory Bird Conservation Act, FLPMA and Wild & Scenic Rivers, plus acquired access and conservation easements and acquired mineral or water interests. Together with [`lua-row`](../lua-row/) (right-of-way corridors) and [`lua-leases-permits-easements`](../lua-leases-permits-easements/) (leases, permits and easements) they complete the surface-use and land-tenure picture around the mineral case records ([`oil-gas-leases`](../oil-gas-leases/), [`mining-claims`](../mining-claims/), [`locatable-operations`](../locatable-operations/)). > ⚠️ **`disp_year` is null on 69% of records.** Only 30,438 of 97,529 carry a disposition date. Any time series here covers a dated minority — see Caveats before building one. - **Source:** BLM National MLRS / EGIS — [`BLM_Natl_MLRS_Acquisitions/FeatureServer/1`](https://gis.blm.gov/nlsdb/rest/services/HUB/BLM_Natl_MLRS_Acquisitions/FeatureServer/1) - **Program:** [BLM Mineral & Land Records System (MLRS)](https://www.blm.gov/services/land-records/mlrs) - **License:** public domain (U.S. Government work — [usa.gov/government-works](https://www.usa.gov/government-works)) - **Extent:** national — 97,529 polygon case records (96,777 geocoded, 752 with no geometry) - **H3:** native resolution 10, parents 9, 8, 0 - **Issue:** [data-workflows #488](https://github.com/boettiger-lab/data-workflows/issues/488) ## Assets | Asset | URL | |---|---| | GeoParquet | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/acquisitions.parquet` | | PMTiles | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/acquisitions.pmtiles` | | H3 hex (res 10) | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/acquisitions/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` | | STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/acquisitions/stac-collection.json` | ## Web map (MapLibre GL JS) The PMTiles **`source-layer` is `acquisitions`**. This is the layer id MapLibre needs; without it the layer renders blank. ```html
``` The `CSE_DISP` match expression colours parcels by status. Note that 'Status Record' — historical entries carried over from the pre-MLRS systems — is the bulk of the layer, so a status-coloured map is dominated by it; filter to 'Authorized' for currently-effective acquisitions. **Do not build a year slider on `disp_year` without handling nulls**: 69% of records have no disposition date and will vanish from any numeric comparison. ## SQL (DuckDB) ```sql INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; -- flat GeoParquet: one row per case record SELECT CSE_NR, BLM_PROD, CSE_DISP, disp_year, RCRD_ACRS, ADMIN_STATE, GEO_STATE FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/acquisitions.parquet') WHERE ADMIN_STATE = 'UT' AND CSE_DISP = 'Authorized' ORDER BY disp_year DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 20; ``` ```sql -- H3 hex: one row per (case, cell). A per-feature total needs a dedup before aggregating. -- ✅ correct — total authorized acreage administered by the Utah state office SELECT SUM(RCRD_ACRS) AS acres FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT _cng_fid, RCRD_ACRS FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/acquisitions/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') WHERE ADMIN_STATE = 'UT' ); -- ❌ wrong — SUM(RCRD_ACRS) straight off the hex multiplies each case by its cell count ``` ```sql -- case density per res-8 cell (h8 is the catalog's universal join key, so this joins -- directly against any other res-8 or finer catalog layer) SELECT h8, COUNT(DISTINCT _cng_fid) AS n_cases FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/acquisitions/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') GROUP BY h8 ORDER BY n_cases DESC LIMIT 10; ``` ## Caveats - **`disp_year` is null on 69% of records (67,091 of 97,529).** Only 30,438 carry a disposition date, mostly outside the 'Status Record' disposition. Any time series covers a dated minority — say so, or exclude the column. - **`PAT_NR` is not a date and no patent year is derivable from it.** Values are General Land Office patent volume/serial strings (`'3 1206'`, `'2 1292C'`), and only 150 of 97,529 records carry one at all. - **752 of 97,529 records have no geometry** (PLSS geocoding of the Legal Land Description failed). Present in the GeoParquet with a null `geom`, absent from PMTiles and H3 hex. - **`RCRD_ACRS` is case-file acreage, not measured polygon area, and is null on 66,921 of 97,529 records.** On the hex it is repeated per cell — dedup by `_cng_fid` before summing; the raw hex sum overstates the total by ~33,900x. - **`REC_TYPE_CSE_GRP` ships inconsistent hyphenation** of the same group (`'Land Tenure - Acquisitions'` vs `'Land Tenure-Acquisitions'`, likewise for `Status`). Values are retained verbatim — normalize before matching or grouping. - **`SUPP_USE` is pipe-delimited and multi-valued** (`'CULTURAL SITES|FEE|RIPARIAN'`), with tokens sometimes repeating inside one value. Split on `|`; equality tests will miss most matches. - **`ADMIN_STATE` is the administering office, not the location** (`ES` = Eastern States, which administers BLM land east of the Mississippi). Use `GEO_STATE` for where the land is — this layer reaches 34 states, well beyond the 12 admin offices. - **`QLTY` was dropped at ingest** — despite its "Data Quality" alias it is a multi-kilobyte dump of the LLD geocoder's debug log. `SRC` is the useful provenance field. ## coal-cases__README.md # BLM National Coal Cases Federal coal leases, licenses, exploration licenses and logical mining units, nationwide, from the Bureau of Land Management's National MLRS / EGIS program — 3,857 polygon cases converted to cloud-native formats (GeoParquet, PMTiles, H3 hex) with parcel-level H3 indexing at resolution 10. Coal is a *leasable* mineral under the Mineral Leasing Act of 1920: the government leases the right to mine rather than allowing it to be claimed. This layer is the federal coal estate's case record — every lease, preference-right lease, exploration license, logical mining unit and prospecting permit BLM administers, with its disposition and acreage. It is the layer to use for questions about coal near the Kaiparowits Plateau and the Grand Staircase-Escalante boundary changes. 971 of 3,857 cases (25.2%) have no geometry — the PLSS geocoder could not place their Legal Land Description. Those rows are retained here in the GeoParquet with a NULL geom but are ABSENT from the PMTiles and the H3 hex, so any area, extent or overlap computed from those two assets omits them. Every case carries a uniform numeric `case_year` (100% populated) for time filtering, with `case_year_src` recording whether that year is the case's effective date or its disposition date. Part of the BLM National MLRS set alongside oil & gas leases, mining claims and locatable-mineral operations. - **Source:** BLM National MLRS / EGIS — `BLM_Natl_MLRS_Coal_Cases/FeatureServer/1` - **Extent:** national · **Features:** 3,857 polygons · **License:** public domain (US federal work) - **H3:** native resolution 10, parents 9, 8, 0 (joins the rest of the catalog at `h8`) - **Tracked in:** [data-workflows #486](https://github.com/boettiger-lab/data-workflows/issues/486) > **971 of 3,857 cases (25.2%) have no geometry.** BLM geocodes these polygons from the Legal Land Description via the PLSS; where that fails the case is kept in the GeoParquet with a NULL `geom` but does not appear in the PMTiles or the H3 hex. Any acreage or overlap computed from those two assets omits them. ## Web map (MapLibre GL JS) The PMTiles `source-layer` is **`coal-cases`** — the last segment of the dataset name. Using anything else renders a blank layer with no error. ```js map.addSource('coal-cases', { type: 'vector', url: 'pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/coal-cases.pmtiles' }); map.addLayer({ id: 'coal-cases-fill', type: 'fill', source: 'coal-cases', 'source-layer': 'coal-cases', // <-- must be exactly this paint: { 'fill-color': ['match', ['get', 'CSE_DISP'], 'Authorized', '#E65100', 'Pending', '#FBC02D', 'Interim', '#8D6E63', 'Closed', '#BDBDBD', '#888888'], 'fill-opacity': 0.4 } }); ``` ## SQL (DuckDB) ```sql INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; -- active cases by state SELECT ADMIN_STATE, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(SUM(RCRD_ACRS)) AS acres FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/coal-cases.parquet') WHERE CSE_DISP = 'Authorized' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY acres DESC; ``` ### Time filtering `case_year` is the uniform numeric year column (100% populated here, range 1908–2026). `case_year_src` says where it came from — `'effective'` (1,263 cases) or `'disposition'` (2,588). They mean different things: an effective year is when a case *started*, a disposition year is usually when it *closed*. For "cases active in year X" use `case_year_src = 'effective'` together with `CSE_DISP`. ```sql SELECT case_year, COUNT(*) AS n FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/coal-cases.parquet') WHERE case_year IS NOT NULL AND case_year_src = 'effective' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1; ``` ### H3 hex One row per (case, H3 cell) at resolution 10. **Case attributes repeat on every cell**, so dedup before summing a per-case total: ```sql -- correct: acreage of authorized cases, deduped SELECT SUM(RCRD_ACRS) FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT _cng_fid, RCRD_ACRS FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/coal-cases/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') WHERE CSE_DISP = 'Authorized'); ``` Join to any other catalog dataset at `h8`. ## geothermal-leases__README.md # BLM National Geothermal Leases Federal geothermal leases and utilization sites, nationwide, from the Bureau of Land Management's National MLRS / EGIS program — 7,394 polygon cases converted to cloud-native formats (GeoParquet, PMTiles, H3 hex) with parcel-level H3 indexing at resolution 10. Geothermal is a leasable energy mineral under the Geothermal Steam Act of 1970. Competitive and noncompetitive leases (pre- and post-2005 terms), converted mining-claimant leases, direct-use leases and utilization sites. Carries FRMTN (the producing formation) and a production status. 195 of 7,394 cases (2.6%) have no geometry — the PLSS geocoder could not place their Legal Land Description. Those rows are retained here in the GeoParquet with a NULL geom but are ABSENT from the PMTiles and the H3 hex, so any area, extent or overlap computed from those two assets omits them. Every case carries a uniform numeric `case_year` (58% populated) for time filtering, with `case_year_src` recording whether that year is the case's effective date or its disposition date. Part of the BLM National MLRS set alongside oil & gas leases, mining claims and locatable-mineral operations. - **Source:** BLM National MLRS / EGIS — `BLM_Natl_MLRS_Geothermal_Leases/FeatureServer/0` - **Extent:** national · **Features:** 7,394 polygons · **License:** public domain (US federal work) - **H3:** native resolution 10, parents 9, 8, 0 (joins the rest of the catalog at `h8`) - **Tracked in:** [data-workflows #486](https://github.com/boettiger-lab/data-workflows/issues/486) > **195 of 7,394 cases (2.6%) have no geometry.** BLM geocodes these polygons from the Legal Land Description via the PLSS; where that fails the case is kept in the GeoParquet with a NULL `geom` but does not appear in the PMTiles or the H3 hex. Any acreage or overlap computed from those two assets omits them. ## Web map (MapLibre GL JS) The PMTiles `source-layer` is **`geothermal-leases`** — the last segment of the dataset name. Using anything else renders a blank layer with no error. ```js map.addSource('geothermal-leases', { type: 'vector', url: 'pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/geothermal-leases.pmtiles' }); map.addLayer({ id: 'geothermal-leases-fill', type: 'fill', source: 'geothermal-leases', 'source-layer': 'geothermal-leases', // <-- must be exactly this paint: { 'fill-color': ['match', ['get', 'CSE_DISP'], 'Authorized', '#E65100', 'Pending', '#FBC02D', 'Interim', '#8D6E63', 'Closed', '#BDBDBD', '#888888'], 'fill-opacity': 0.4 } }); ``` ## SQL (DuckDB) ```sql INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; -- active cases by state SELECT ADMIN_STATE, COUNT(*) AS cases, ROUND(SUM(RCRD_ACRS)) AS acres FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/geothermal-leases.parquet') WHERE CSE_DISP = 'Authorized' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY acres DESC; ``` ### Time filtering `case_year` is the uniform numeric year column (58% populated here, range 1974–2026). `case_year_src` says where it came from — `'effective'` (4,299 cases) or `'disposition'` (0). They mean different things: an effective year is when a case *started*, a disposition year is usually when it *closed*. For "cases active in year X" use `case_year_src = 'effective'` together with `CSE_DISP`. ```sql SELECT case_year, COUNT(*) AS n FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/geothermal-leases.parquet') WHERE case_year IS NOT NULL AND case_year_src = 'effective' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1; ``` ### H3 hex One row per (case, H3 cell) at resolution 10. **Case attributes repeat on every cell**, so dedup before summing a per-case total: ```sql -- correct: acreage of authorized cases, deduped SELECT SUM(RCRD_ACRS) FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT _cng_fid, RCRD_ACRS FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/geothermal-leases/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') WHERE CSE_DISP = 'Authorized'); ``` Join to any other catalog dataset at `h8`. ## grazing-allotments__README.md # BLM National Grazing Allotments Where the Bureau of Land Management authorises livestock grazing on public rangeland. 21,252 boundary polygons representing 20,966 allotments across the ten western state offices, converted to GeoParquet, PMTiles and H3 hex. An allotment is a **management unit, not a parcel of federal land**. A boundary drawn here can enclose private, state and other federal land alongside the BLM land inside it, so the area of an allotment is not the area of public land being grazed. Answering how much federal land an allotment covers means intersecting these boundaries with a surface-ownership layer such as PAD-US. The publisher describes this layer as *supplemental to the Rangeland Administration System (RAS), which is authoritative for BLM grazing allotments (except Alaska)*, and as *a subset of the official national dataset, containing features and attributes intended for public release*. What is public here is geometry and administrative identifiers. ## What is not in this layer Animal unit months, permittees and seasons of use are **not** published in this feature class. They live in RAS as tabular reports at [reports.blm.gov](https://reports.blm.gov), joined to these boundaries on `ST_ALLOT`, the RAS allotment key. `ST_ALLOT` is usually `ADMIN_ST` followed by `ALLOT_NO`, but 29 polygons disagree with those two columns, so join on `ST_ALLOT` itself. ## Coverage The ten western state offices: Arizona, California, Colorado, Idaho, Montana, New Mexico, Nevada, Oregon, Utah and Wyoming. Despite RAS carving out Alaska, no Alaskan allotment appears in this layer. Bounding box 124.5W to 98.9W, 31.3N to 49.0N. | `ADMIN_ST` | office | polygons | allotments | acres | |---|---|---|---|---| | `MT` | Montana | 5,277 | 5,223 | 26,549,430 | | `WY` | Wyoming | 3,560 | 3,556 | 32,364,576 | | `CO` | Colorado | 2,399 | 2,299 | 10,315,186 | | `NM` | New Mexico | 2,250 | 2,240 | 26,619,704 | | `ID` | Idaho | 2,072 | 2,072 | 15,051,372 | | `OR` | Oregon | 1,922 | 1,921 | 18,883,780 | | `UT` | Utah | 1,414 | 1,401 | 27,463,072 | | `AZ` | Arizona | 869 | 819 | 19,769,331 | | `NV` | Nevada | 759 | 757 | 48,073,478 | | `CA` | California | 728 | 677 | 7,880,610 | | (null) | | 2 | 2 | 1,786 | The polygons column counts every row. Allotments and acres exclude the 34 placeholder polygons, as the first query below does. ### `ADMIN_ST` is the administering office, not the state the land is in State offices administer across state lines. 1,084 allotments have their centre in a different state than `ADMIN_ST` names: | administered by | land lies in | allotments | |---|---|---| | `MT` | South Dakota | 510 | | `OR` | Washington | 369 | | `MT` | North Dakota | 82 | | `CA` | Nevada | 31 | | `WY` | Nebraska | 18 | | | 17 other pairs | 74 | South Dakota, North Dakota, Washington and Nebraska have no state office of their own here, so filtering `ADMIN_ST = 'SD'` returns nothing while 510 allotments sit in South Dakota. **Selecting allotments by the state they are in needs an intersection with a state boundary layer, not a filter on `ADMIN_ST`.** ## One allotment can be several polygons 137 `ST_ALLOT` keys span 389 polygons, each polygon carrying its own `GIS_ACRES`. 35 of those keys carry more than one `ALLOT_NAME`: mostly spelling variants such as Wheatley A and Wheately A, but some look like distinct allotments sharing a key, such as Zuni Ranch and Concho Ranch on `AZ06170`. On the GeoParquet the acreage of an allotment is the **sum** over its polygons; deduplicating would undercount. On the hex the opposite holds, because every attribute is repeated per cell. ## Assets | Asset | URL | |---|---| | GeoParquet | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/grazing-allotments.parquet` | | PMTiles | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/grazing-allotments.pmtiles` | | H3 hex | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/grazing-allotments/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet` | | STAC | `https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/grazing-allotments/stac-collection.json` | ## DuckDB ```sql INSTALL spatial; LOAD spatial; INSTALL httpfs; LOAD httpfs; -- allotments and acreage by administering state office SELECT ADMIN_ST, COUNT(DISTINCT ST_ALLOT) AS allotments, ROUND(SUM(GIS_ACRES)) AS acres FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/grazing-allotments.parquet') WHERE ST_ALLOT <> '' AND ST_ALLOT NOT LIKE '%00000' AND ST_ALLOT <> 'MTUNK' -- drop placeholders GROUP BY ADMIN_ST ORDER BY acres DESC; -- acreage of each allotment, summing the polygons it is stored as SELECT ST_ALLOT, ALLOT_NAME, COUNT(*) AS polygons, SUM(GIS_ACRES) AS acres FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/grazing-allotments.parquet') WHERE ST_ALLOT <> '' AND ST_ALLOT NOT LIKE '%00000' AND ST_ALLOT <> 'MTUNK' -- drop placeholders GROUP BY ST_ALLOT, ALLOT_NAME ORDER BY acres DESC LIMIT 10; -- the 1,401 allotments administered by the Utah state office, as 1,414 polygons SELECT ALLOT_NO, ALLOT_NAME, ADM_UNIT_CD, ROUND(GIS_ACRES) AS acres FROM read_parquet('https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/grazing-allotments.parquet') WHERE ADMIN_ST = 'UT' ORDER BY acres DESC; ``` ### H3 hex One row per polygon and H3 cell pair at native resolution 8 (about 0.74 km² per cell), with `h0` as the hive partition key. 1,215,430 rows over 1,212,096 distinct resolution 8 cells, covering all 21,252 polygons. Resolution 8 suits the grain: the median allotment is about 12 km², and nothing finer is supportable from boundaries drawn at this scale. `h8` is the catalog's universal join key, so these allotments join directly to any other resolution 8 hex dataset. Every attribute is repeated on every cell the polygon covers, so `GIS_ACRES` must be deduplicated by `_cng_fid` before it is summed, and allotment counts use `COUNT(DISTINCT ST_ALLOT)`: ```sql -- correct: one acreage value per polygon SELECT SUM(GIS_ACRES) FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT _cng_fid, GIS_ACRES FROM read_parquet('s3://public-blm/grazing-allotments/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') WHERE ADMIN_ST = 'UT'); -- wrong: SUM(GIS_ACRES) over hex rows multiplies each polygon by its cell count ``` ```sql -- allotment land overlapping another resolution 8 dataset, joined on h8 SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.h8) AS shared_cells FROM read_parquet('s3://public-blm/grazing-allotments/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') a JOIN read_parquet('s3:////hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') b USING (h8); ``` ## MapLibre GL JS The PMTiles `source-layer` is **`grazing-allotments`**. ```js import * as pmtiles from 'pmtiles'; const protocol = new pmtiles.Protocol(); maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', protocol.tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/positron-gl-style/style.json', center: [-110.0, 42.0], zoom: 5 }); map.on('load', () => { map.addSource('allotments', { type: 'vector', url: 'pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/grazing-allotments.pmtiles' }); map.addLayer({ id: 'allotments-fill', type: 'fill', source: 'allotments', 'source-layer': 'grazing-allotments', // = last segment of the dataset name paint: { 'fill-color': '#8c6d3f', 'fill-opacity': 0.35 } }); map.addLayer({ id: 'allotments-line', type: 'line', source: 'allotments', 'source-layer': 'grazing-allotments', paint: { 'line-color': '#732600', 'line-width': 0.6 } }); }); ``` ## Known quirks, published as the source records them - `ACTIVE_DT` is mostly a placeholder, not a per-allotment date. 11,892 polygons have no usable value (the source carries the impossible years 0999 and 9999 there, published here as null), 4,648 carry 1934-06-28 (the Taylor Grazing Act), 3,493 carry 1899-12-30 and 237 carry 1946-01-01. Only about 1,000 polygons carry a date that plausibly describes the allotment. - `ALLOT_NO` is unique only within a state office, and `ADMIN_ST` plus `ALLOT_NO` does not always reproduce `ST_ALLOT`. Use `ST_ALLOT` to identify an allotment. `ALLOT_NO` is usually five digits, with exceptions: `UNK` and `Unk`, `142`, `1601`, twelve `MCG01`-style codes, and one empty value. - 34 polygons carry a placeholder `ST_ALLOT` instead of an allotment key: empty, `XX00000`, `AZ00000`, `CO00000`, `MT00000`, `NM00000`, `OR00000` or `MTUNK`. Exclude them before counting or totalling allotments. - 19 polygons carry `ALLOT_NO = '00000'` and names like `Private or State`, `Unalloted` or `None`. These mark land inside an allotment boundary that is not itself allotted. - `GIS_ACRES` is 0 on six polygons and below 1 acre on eleven. - 37 features are geometry collections in which a degenerate line accompanies the polygon. All geometries are valid; the rest are polygons (17,389) and multipolygons (3,826). - `OGC_FID` is an artifact of the format conversion and carries no meaning from the source. Use `_cng_fid` (one per polygon) or `GlobalID` (the stable upstream identifier). - `SHAPE_Length` and `SHAPE_Area` from the service were dropped: they are decimal-degree values, not real measurements. The real area is `GIS_ACRES`. ## Provenance and license Public domain. The layer's own metadata records the use constraint as *"None, these data are considered public domain"*. The service's copyright text, *"Compiled by the Bureau of Land Management (BLM), Headquarters (HQ)"*, is an attribution string, not a restriction. Credit: BLM administering state offices. The source is a live ArcGIS map service with no published version or release date, so the access date is the only edition marker. This snapshot was read on **2026-09-22** from layer 12 (*Grazing Allotment Polygons*) of the [BLM National Grazing Allotment MapServer](https://gis.blm.gov/arcgis/rest/services/range/BLM_Natl_Grazing_Allotment/MapServer/12), whose landing page is [BLM Natl Grazing Allotment Polygons](https://gbp-blm-egis.hub.arcgis.com/datasets/BLM-EGIS::blm-natl-grazing-allotment-polygons). The service's own edit stamps in this snapshot run from 2026-08-13 to 2026-09-21. The raw GeoJSON scraped from the service is kept at `s3://public-blm/raw/grazing-allotments.geojson` (140,547,548 bytes, sha256 `cd7638821289a3c290e09adc429b9660d7fb7324b4373880290b72412790d5b0`). Because the service is overwritten in place, that stored copy and its checksum are what makes this edition resolvable later. The service publishes in EPSG:3857 over a source in EPSG:4269 (NAD83); the scrape requested EPSG:4326 directly, at the source's own coordinate tolerance, so the published data is WGS84 with no further reprojection. ## locatable-operations__README.md # BLM National MLRS Locatable-Mineral Operations Federal **locatable-mineral (hard-rock) surface-management operations** — Notices and Plans of Operations under the General Mining Law of 1872 — nationwide, from the Bureau of Land Management's National MLRS / EGIS program. **2,399** polygon features across 11 western BLM states, converted to cloud-native formats (GeoParquet, PMTiles, H3 hex) with parcel-level H3 indexing at **resolution 10**. The two MLRS operation-level service layers are unioned into one collection: **1,264 Notices** (≤ 5-acre disturbance, notice-level) + **1,135 Plans of Operations** (larger disturbance, plan-level). The derived **`op_level`** column (`Notice` / `Plan of Operations`) makes the two levels filterable. Licence: public domain, as a US federal government work (https://www.usa.gov/government-works). ## utah-federal-mineral-estate__README.md # BLM Utah Federal Mineral Estate The federal mineral estate in Utah: which parcels carry federally owned minerals, and which commodity classes those minerals fall into. 101,585 polygon parcels published by the Bureau of Land Management Utah State Office, converted to GeoParquet, PMTiles and H3 hex. This is *ownership of the mineral estate*, which is different from the *rights granted* on it that the BLM mineral case and lease collections record. Utah is heavily split estate, so owning or managing the surface does not imply owning the minerals underneath: 12,183 of these parcels carry federally owned minerals under surface administered by someone other than the federal government or the BLM. The grain is the survey subdivision, not a lease or a case. Each parcel is a Public Land Survey System aliquot part identified by `GCDBDIVID`, commonly about 40 acres. ## Commodity flags Commodity membership is carried as ten independent flag columns rather than as ten separate layers. The source service publishes one feature class through eleven definition-query views, and a parcel can appear in several of them, so the per-commodity view counts total 106,444 against 101,585 parcels. 3,247 parcels carry more than one commodity flag and 158 carry none. the one parcel with no geometry in the source cannot be hexed. Every parcel attribute is repeated on every cell the parcel covers, so `GIS_Acres` must be deduplicated by `_cng_fid` before it is summed, and parcel counts use `COUNT(DISTINCT _cng_fid)`: ```sql -- correct: one acreage value per parcel SELECT SUM(GIS_Acres) FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT _cng_fid, GIS_Acres FROM read_parquet('s3://public-blm/utah-federal-mineral-estate/hex/h0=*/data_0.parquet') WHERE Coal IS NOT NULL); -- wrong: SUM(GIS_Acres) over hex rows multiplies each parcel by its cell count ``` ## MapLibre GL JS The PMTiles `source-layer` is **`utah-federal-mineral-estate`**. ```js import * as pmtiles from 'pmtiles'; const protocol = new pmtiles.Protocol(); maplibregl.addProtocol('pmtiles', protocol.tile); const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://basemaps.cartocdn.com/gl/positron-gl-style/style.json', center: [-111.5, 39.3], zoom: 6 }); map.on('load', () => { map.addSource('mineral-estate', { type: 'vector', url: 'pmtiles://https://s3-west.nrp-nautilus.io/public-blm/utah-federal-mineral-estate.pmtiles' }); map.addLayer({ id: 'coal', type: 'fill', source: 'mineral-estate', 'source-layer': 'utah-federal-mineral-estate', // = last segment of the dataset name filter: ['has', 'Coal'], paint: { 'fill-color': '#4a3728', 'fill-opacity': 0.6 } }); }); ``` ## Known quirks, published as the source records them - `Section_` valid PLSS sections run 1 to 36 (100,908 parcels).
